title: Applying the Learning Sciences
description: Ground design decisions in how people actually learn — memory, cognitive load, motivation, and transfer — rather than intuition or tradition.
pedagogy: Evidence-informed design: each instructional choice is justified by a learning-science principle and treated as a testable hypothesis, echoing the LEAMM competency model's 'learning science application' domain.

title: Human-Centered Design
description: Design learning experiences around real learners and their contexts, integrating human factors and iterative needs analysis into every LE project.
pedagogy: Design-thinking and human-systems-integration practice: empathize, prototype, and test with learners in the loop before committing to a solution.

title: Data Instrumentation & Analytics
description: Instrument learning environments and turn the resulting data into evidence — through measurement design, educational data mining, and learning analytics.
pedagogy: Formative, data-driven improvement: build measurement in from the start so learning can be observed, debugged, and improved on evidence.

title: Competency Frameworks & Knowledge Representation
description: Structure what learners should know and be able to do into interoperable competency frameworks, learning objectives, and machine-readable standards.
pedagogy: Competency-based design: outcomes are defined explicitly and portably (per IEEE 1484.20.2 and CASE) so assessment, credentialing, and adaptivity can all reference the same shared model.

title: Lean-Agile Methods & Systems Thinking
description: Run learning-engineering work as iterative, decision-tracked cycles and reason about the whole learning system, not isolated interventions.
pedagogy: Lean-agile delivery: short build-measure-learn loops with documented decisions, so the process itself is inspectable and continuously improved.
